rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE on a GATING HIGH from bug_historian. That objection was correct, it is FIXED IN CODE, and a second objection (prior_art_librarian) forced me to RETRACT my headline evidence. Both are below, then the original rationale carried forward.

(A) bug_historian [HIGH, GATING] — "the zero-rows path returns an error, and by verifiers.go's documented fail-open policy an errored verifier does not block completion, so complete_work_item still stamps the item complete. That is CLOSED 032's shape and symptom-2 reproduced through the NEW verifier's own error branch." CORRECT, AND DAMNING, AND FIXED. I had written 'I am aware this means the caller fails open on that path' and shipped it anyway — naming a defect is not a control on it, which is a lesson this very estate has a WRONG_CALLS entry for. The error branch delivered exactly the outcome the verifier exists to prevent, on the ONE input where the ambiguous case IS content loss. The zero-rows path now returns Resolved:false, which BLOCKS completion and routes the item to attempts and then human review. An unverifiable page is not a repaired page. The test now asserts the ABSENCE of an error as well as Resolved==false, so reintroducing the error branch fails the build; proven by mutation (Resolved:true there fails RefusesToCertifyAnEmptyPage).

(B) prior_art_librarian [MEDIUM] — "the load-bearing live instance is gaswholesalers.com/how-pricing-works, and this exact page+site is named in a LANDMINE about the content_data envelope guard refusing one live page on purpose; rule it out before the council trusts the evidence." CHECKED, AND THE OBJECTION LANDS. That component matches the landmine's own detector exactly: content_data->>'type'='text' AND jsonb_typeof(content_data->'result')='string'. The markdown I found sits inside an UNDECODED LLM transport envelope, so the item reaching 'complete' with markdown intact may be explained by the envelope guard refusing to normalise rather than by a handler writing nothing. I HAVE RETRACTED the claim in bugs_open/201 rather than defend it. It also has a consequence beyond me: this is the only 'complete' literal_markdown item in existence, so 201's own §Symptom-2 section rests on the same row, and I have flagged that for whoever works it next rather than overturning a filer's artefact-level work I have not repeated. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: symptom 2's mechanism is established from CODE — mark_complete passes handler_result with no write-check, and the registry existed with this item_type unregistered. The fix never depended on that page.

(C) guardian [MEDIUM] — "the verifier is registered against item_type alone, not handler_agent; the whole-page remit argument is built on page-build-handler, but 14 literal_markdown rows carry handler_agent='page-content-writer', a narrower-remit handler." MEASURED, and it is NOT live today: all 12 page-content-writer rows are terminal (1 complete, 11 failed), none claimable; the only non-terminal row is the new detected one at page-build-handler. But the seat is right that it COULD become live, because 201's own verify recipe contemplates re-arming those failed rows. The operational guard already exists and is written down: bugs_open/201's RUNBOOK R6 trap 1 says a re-arm must also set handler_agent, or it re-runs the broken route. I have NOT added a handler_agent check to the verifier: VerifyTarget does not carry handler_agent, so it would mean widening a shared contract to defend against a state the estate already forbids operationally. Stated so the choice is visible rather than silent.

(D) editquality [MEDIUM] — the RFC_010 retraction-seam landmines: is literal_markdown filed from more than one place, and does Run() have a mid-loop early-exit that makes retraction inert? SINGLE PRODUCER, stated in the file's own header and traceable to owner ruling 2026-08-02 point 1 and concept-register CQ-019: "Producer set for this item_type: this check alone." On the early-exit: this check has NO monotonic early return — its header records that the guard `if len(sections)==0 { return }` was deliberately REMOVED from the sibling check_empty_sections for exactly this reason, and check_literal_markdown was written after that lesson; its retraction gate is scannedPages, which is populated per row before any finding test. Note also that THIS SUBMISSION DOES NOT TOUCH THE RETRACTION SEAM — it adds a completion verifier, a different mechanism — but the seat was right that the landmine cluster matches the file being edited and should be answered rather than assumed.

(E) debug_historian [MEDIUM x2, LOW] on migration 331 — (i) "no visible BEGIN/ROLLBACK wrapper": the objection is against my SKETCH, which elided it; the actual file opens with `\set ON_ERROR_STOP on` then `BEGIN;` and closes `COMMIT;`, same shape as precedent 322. Sketch corrected below. (ii) "the migration number is claimed by filename only, with no check against schema_migrations": fair at submission time, and now discharged by evidence rather than argument — 331 was applied THROUGH run-migrations.sh and the ledger records it (schema_migrations, 2026-08-07 01:29:01Z), with no other 33x row. ⚠ And a finding the seat's concern surfaced: a plain `--apply` would have been WRONG here — 19 other lanes' files are pending, and 305 probes inconclusive (its live pre_query has drifted from the 4-entry list it expects) so it would have FAILED and stopped the run before ever reaching 331. I scoped MIGRATIONS_DIR to a one-file directory. (iii) "no separate rollback artefact": correct, house style wants it distinct; 331_..._ROLLBACK.sql added.

(F) guardian [LOW] — "the migration mutates a fleet-wide scheduler predicate and should be flagged as shared infrastructure rather than treated as a same-tier discovery_checks change." Accepted as stated; it is flagged as such here and in the file header. The read-before-write plus RAISE-on-mismatch containment the seat credits is unchanged.

--- ORIGINAL RATIONALE, carried forward because each round is judged standalone ---

bugs_open/201 SYMPTOM 2, the half deliberately left until fix-1 was proven (201 §2 says fixing it first would make the BROKEN routing look repaired; fix-1 is now proven live — a sweep on v1.0.1257 filed a literal_markdown item carrying handler_agent=page-build-handler, item d2a6117d, 2026-08-06 11:34:22Z).

THE DEFECT. complete_work_item stamps an item 'complete' on the handler saga's own word. A saga can 'succeed' without touching the defect — verifiers.go's own header names the mechanism (page-build-handler's complete_error path is a success-labelled complete_workflow). Live instance, found in the pre-flight for fix-1's proof and not looked for: gaswholesalers.com's existing literal_markdown item reads status='complete' while `**Decision Engine**` is STILL in content_data on the page it names (how-pricing-works, slot pricing). That is symptom 2 reproduced two days after filing, on the same site used to prove the other half.

WHY A VERIFIER RATHER THAN A NEW MECHANISM. The estate already has exactly this: ItemVerifier / RegisterVerifier (verifiers.go), consulted by CompleteWorkItemAction before stamping, with seven verifiers registered and a coverage guard that tracks which item types lack one. literal_markdown was already ON that backlog with a written deferral note. So this is filling a declared gap with the established mechanism — no new seam, no new contract, no new table. 201 §4 candidate 3 asked for symptom 2 to be 'diagnosed separately'; this is that, for the item type 201 is about. It does NOT change complete_work_item's general trust of handler_result — every other unverified item type is exactly as it was.

THE REMIT TEST, WHICH IS THE ONE WAY THIS COULD BE WRONG. verifier_coverage_test.go's page_rerender entry is the estate's cautionary tale: a working verifier was written and deliberately HELD because re-running the detector's predicate over the whole page is STRICTER THAN THE HANDLER'S REMIT, which would mark correctly-handled items unresolved, burn their attempts and strand 1,849 of them in 'failed'. The literal_markdown deferral note carried the same warning forward verbatim: 'write it against the REPAIRING agent's rewrite remit, not the detector's predicate'. I followed it. This item's handler is page-build-handler (re-pointed by fix-1), whose build_pages_loop runs load_spec_sections -> plan_sections and rewrites ALL of the page's spec sections. So whole-page scope IS its remit — not more. And unlike page_rerender there is no designed two-strike escalation to destroy: a failed verify routes to the attempt machinery and then human review, which is the right destination for a markdown defect the writer did not clear.

THE ZERO-ROWS CASE, which is where I expect scrutiny and where I chose to refuse rather than certify. If the page has no scannable components the scan finds no markdown — and that observation is identical whether the page was repaired or its content was LOST. bugs_closed/194's damage class is exactly that: 31 of 106 components NULL on one live site. Reporting Resolved there would stamp 'complete' over a destroyed page. The verifier returns an error instead ('cannot distinguish repaired from content lost'), which CompleteWorkItemAction records rather than silently treating as success. I am aware this means the caller fails open on that path — that is the registry's existing documented policy (verifiers.go:60-63) and I did not invent a different one for this verifier; changing it would be a change to every verifier, which is not this bug's scope.

DRIFT. verifiers.go's contract is that a verifier re-runs 'the SAME predicate the discovery check used to create the item'. Two hand-kept copies of a five-line scan is precisely how that stops being true, so the per-row scan is EXTRACTED into scanComponentRowForMarkdown and both the detector and the verifier call it. The row SELECTION is still written twice because the scopes genuinely differ (site-wide vs page-scoped); their WHERE clauses are otherwise identical (locked_at IS NULL, plus the both-surfaces-empty exclusion) and a comment says they must stay so.

THE TWO NON-OBVIOUS OBLIGATIONS, both discharged. Registering a verifier is NOT what makes it gate: the claimed-item-timeout sweep auto-completes a stuck item at 15 minutes on the handler orchestration's own evidence, walking straight past the verifier, unless the item_type is in that sweep's `item_type NOT IN (...)` list. TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion failed the moment I registered and named the obligation — the designed catch, and it worked. The half the test CANNOT check is that the file it reads (220) is only the DECLARED list; the LIVE scheduled_tasks.pre_query is a separate edit, and a lane has already declared an entry that never reached the live column, leaving their verifier bypassable for two days. So this ships BOTH: 220 updated, and migration 331 for the live column, written against the exact current string after reading it.

plan.summary: bugs_open/201 symptom 2: a handler saga can report success having written nothing and complete_work_item stamps the item 'complete' on its word — proven live on gaswholesalers.com, whose literal_markdown item reads 'complete' while the markdown is still in content_data. Register an ItemVerifier for literal_markdown using the estate's existing completion-verification mechanism, re-running the detector's own predicate page-scoped. Extract the per-row scan so detector and verifier cannot drift, refuse to certify a page with no scannable components (that observation cannot distinguish 'repaired' from bugs_closed/194's content loss), and discharge both halves of the claim-timeout lockstep so the sweep cannot auto-complete past the new verifier.

edits.rationale: Registers the verifier, extracts the shared per-row predicate so the detector and the verifier cannot drift (verifiers.go's stated contract), and adds the verifier itself. Whole-page scope is deliberate and matches page-build-handler's remit — the one way this could be wrong is being stricter than the handler, which is the page_rerender trap the deferral note warned about. Zero scannable rows returns an ERROR, not Resolved, because that observation cannot distinguish a repaired page from one whose components were lost. ROUND 2, THE GATING FIX: the zero-rows branch returns Resolved:false, NOT an error. The registry fails open on error (verifiers.go:60-63), so the r1 error branch would have stamped 'complete' on exactly the content-loss case it was written to protect — bugs_closed/032's shape, and symptom 2 reproduced through the new guard.

The load-bearing assertion is the UNRESOLVED case — a verifier that always returned Resolved would pass a happy-path test. Proven to bite by mutation: with the Resolved branch made unconditional, TestVerifyLiteralMarkdownResolved_RefusesWhenMarkdownSurvives FAILS; restored, the package is ok. Also pins the shared predicate against the check's documented false-positive guards (arithmetic is not bold; a markup-bearing value's backticks are code).

The coverage guard failed on registration with 'HAS a verifier but is still listed as a gap — remove it from itemTypesWithoutVerifiers'. Removing the entry is what the guard demands. Replaced with a comment recording that the deferral note's instruction (write against the handler's remit, not the detector's predicate) was actually followed and why whole-page scope satisfies it, so the reasoning survives the entry's deletion. Remaining diff in this file is gofmt realignment after the longest key was removed.

edits.rationale: Half one of the lockstep. TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion reads this file and failed on registration: the claimed-item-timeout sweep auto-completes at 15 minutes on handler-orchestration evidence alone, bypassing any verifier whose item_type is not excluded here.

edits.rationale: Half two, and the half no test can check: 220 is only the DECLARED list; the LIVE column is a separate edit. 305's header records a lane declaring an entry that never reached the live column, leaving their verifier bypassable for two days. Live column read BEFORE writing the replace (the LANDMINES requirement) — exactly one row, seven entries, identical to 220, so no drift is carried. Asserts both directions in DO/RAISE blocks, because a verify block of plain SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT. ROUND 2: the r1 sketch elided the transaction bracketing and drew an objection for it — the file always had `\set ON_ERROR_STOP on` + BEGIN;/COMMIT;, shown now. Applied through run-migrations.sh and recorded in the ledger; a plain --apply would have been wrong (19 other lanes pending; 305 probes inconclusive and would have halted the run first), so MIGRATIONS_DIR was scoped to one file.

ROUND 2, at debug_historian's LOW objection: the needle-gate discipline wants rollback as a DISTINCT artefact, not inline post-verify blocks bundled with the forward migration (211 is the house precedent). UPPERCASE sidecars are excluded from run-migrations.sh by SIDECAR_RE and run by hand. Its header states the thing a future operator most needs to know: rolling back RE-ARMS the bypass, so prefer fixing or unregistering the verifier over restoring it.

grounded_in: R2 GATING FIX PROVEN BY MUTATION: with the zero-rows branch returning Resolved:true, go test -run LiteralMarkdown FAILS — 'Resolved=true for a page with no scannable components — that certifies bugs_closed/194's content-loss class as a successful repair'. Restored, the package is ok. The test also asserts err==nil, so reintroducing the r1 error branch fails the build too.

R2 RETRACTION, MEASURED: gaswholesalers.com/how-pricing-works slot 'pricing' returns content_data->>'type'='text' AND jsonb_typeof(content_data->'result')='string' — the envelope-guard landmine's own detector query, matched exactly. The cited markdown is inside an undecoded transport envelope. The claim is retracted in bugs_open/201 with a visible correction rather than quietly dropped.

R2 GUARDIAN CHECK, MEASURED: SELECT handler_agent, status, claimed_by IS NOT NULL, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='literal_markdown' GROUP BY 1,2,3 => page-build-handler|detected|f|1 ;; page-content-writer|complete|t|1 ;; page-content-writer|failed|t|11. All 12 pre-fix rows terminal; the remit mismatch is not live today, and RUNBOOK R6 trap 1 already requires a re-arm to set handler_agent.

R2 LEDGER CHECK: SELECT filename, applied_at FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename LIKE '33%' => exactly one row, 331_literal_markdown_claim_timeout_exclusion.sql, 2026-08-07 01:29:01Z. Applied through run-migrations.sh, not a bare psql -f.

R2 LIVE COLUMN VERIFIED AFTER APPLY, at the artefact rather than the runner's output: the live pre_query now reads item_type NOT IN ('truncated_component', 'hardcoded_section_colors', 'empty_section', 'orphan_element_refs', 'content_duplication', 'page_canonical_collision', 'dead_fragment_link', 'literal_markdown'), and the old 7-entry string is consumed (both asserted separately).

R2 SINGLE-PRODUCER CHECK for editquality: check_literal_markdown.go's header states 'Producer set for this item_type: this check alone (owner ruling 2026-08-02 point 1 — stated in the concept-register entry, CQ-019)'. And this submission does not touch the retraction seam at all — it adds a completion verifier.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND THIS TYPE WAS ON ITS BACKLOG: verifiers.go declares ItemVerifier/RegisterVerifier/GetVerifier, CompleteWorkItemAction consults the registry before stamping, seven verifiers are registered today, and literal_markdown was already listed in itemTypesWithoutVerifiers with a written deferral note. No new mechanism is proposed.

THE REMIT ARGUMENT, from the handler's live step graph: page-build-handler runs ensure_site_record -> load_page_record -> load_existing_content -> load_spec_sections -> plan_sections -> ... -> save_sections, where load_spec_sections is load_page_sections_from_spec ('Load sections from site_specs.site_plan (authoritative), fall back to pages.sections'). It rewrites the page's spec sections, so whole-page verification is its remit and not stricter.

THE TRAP THIS AVOIDS, quoted from verifier_coverage_test.go's page_rerender entry: a whole-page verifier there 'would mark a correctly-handled rerender unresolved, burn its attempts and strand it in failed, destroying that designed escalation across 1,849 items'. Unlike page_rerender there is no designed two-strike escalation on this type to destroy.

THE ZERO-ROWS JUSTIFICATION IS MEASURED: bugs_closed/194 §4 and this lane's census of ai-agent-orchestration.com — 31 of 106 page_components carry NULL content_data across 10 pages, every component on 9 of them. A page in that state scans clean.

BOTH LOCKSTEP GUARDS FIRED ON REGISTRATION, the designed catch working: TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap ('HAS a verifier but is still listed as a gap'), and TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion ('HAS a Go verifier but is NOT excluded in 220 ... the claimed-item-timeout sweep will auto-complete it on handler-orchestration evidence alone, bypassing the verifier').

SHARED-TREE CHECK: git archive HEAD extracted clean, overlaid with only these files, go build ./platform/... succeeds and the package tests pass. The FIRST archive run FAILED because only the Go files were copied — independent evidence that the lockstep test really reads 220_*.sql from disk rather than being decorative.

SCOPE LIMIT UNCHANGED: nothing here alters complete_work_item's general trust of handler_result, and every other unverified item_type behaves exactly as before. bug_historian's MISSING note — whether verifiers.go's fail-open-on-error policy has ever been raised to the council as its own architecture item — is surfaced to the owner rather than answered here, because changing it changes every verifier.
